passages.text: Fourteen years later I went up again to Jerusalem, accompanied by Barnabas. I took Titus along also.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian leader and former persecutor of Christians.
Fourteen years passed.
I went up again to Jerusalem.
Barnabas went with me.
I also took Titus with me.
passages.original: Ἔπειτα διὰ δεκατεσσάρων ἐτῶν πάλιν ἀνέβην εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα μετὰ Βαρνάβα συμπαραλαβὼν καὶ Τίτον

passages.text: I went in response to a revelation and set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders, for fear that I was running or had already run in vain.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
God gave Paul a revelation.
Paul went to Jerusalem because of this revelation.
Paul explained the gospel to the people in Jerusalem.
Paul preached this gospel among the Gentiles.
Paul spoke privately to the recognized leaders in Jerusalem.
Paul did this to make sure his work was not in vain.
Paul wanted to confirm that he was not running his race for nothing.
passages.original: ἀνέβην δὲ κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν καὶ ἀνεθέμην αὐτοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ κηρύσσω ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν κατ’ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς δοκοῦσιν μή πως εἰς κενὸν τρέχω ἢ ἔδραμον

passages.text: Yet not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek.
passages.sermon:
Titus was with me.
Titus was a Greek.
No one forced Titus to be circumcised.
Titus did not have to be circumcised.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ Τίτος ὁ σὺν ἐμοί Ἕλλην ὤν ἠναγκάσθη περιτμηθῆναι

passages.text: This issue arose because some false brothers had come in under false pretenses to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us.
passages.sermon:
Some men pretended to be brothers.
They were not true believers.
They came in secretly.
They wanted to watch us.
We have freedom in Christ Jesus.
These men wanted to take away our freedom.
They wanted to make us slaves.
passages.original: διὰ δὲ τοὺς παρεισάκτους ψευδαδέλφους οἵτινες παρεισῆλθον κατασκοπῆσαι τὴν ἐλευθερίαν ἡμῶν ἣν ἔχομεν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἵνα ἡμᾶς καταδουλώσουσιν

passages.text: We did not give in to them for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.
passages.sermon:
We did not give in to these false brothers.
We did not submit to them, even for a moment.
We did this so the truth of the gospel would remain with you.
passages.original: οἷς οὐδὲ πρὸς ὥραν εἴξαμεν τῇ ὑποταγῇ ἵνα ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ εὐαγγελίου διαμείνῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: But as for the highly esteemed—whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism —those leaders added nothing to me.
passages.sermon:
Some people were considered highly esteemed leaders.
Their past or status does not matter to me.
God does not show favoritism to anyone.
These leaders did not add anything to my message.
passages.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν δοκούντων εἶναί τι ὁποῖοί ποτε ἦσαν οὐδέν μοι διαφέρει πρόσωπον ὁ Θεὸς ἀνθρώπου οὐ λαμβάνει ἐμοὶ γὰρ οἱ δοκοῦντες οὐδὲν προσανέθεντο

passages.text: On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted to preach the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle.
\r\nGod gave Paul a special task.
\r\nGod entrusted Paul with the gospel for the uncircumcised.
\r\nThe uncircumcised are Gentiles.
\r\nPeter was also an apostle.
\r\nGod entrusted Peter with the gospel for the circumcised.
\r\nThe circumcised are Jews.
\r\nThe leaders saw this.
\r\nThe leaders saw that God gave Paul the gospel for the Gentiles.
\r\nThe leaders saw that God gave Peter the gospel for the Jews.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ τοὐναντίον ἰδόντες ὅτι πεπίστευμαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἀκροβυστίας καθὼς Πέτρος τῆς περιτομῆς

passages.text: For the One who was at work in Peter’s apostleship to the circumcised was also at work in my apostleship to the Gentiles.
passages.sermon:
God worked through Peter.
Peter was an apostle to the circumcised.
God also worked through me.
I am an apostle to the Gentiles.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ ἐνεργήσας Πέτρῳ εἰς ἀποστολὴν τῆς περιτομῆς ἐνήργησεν καὶ ἐμοὶ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη

passages.text: And recognizing the grace that I had been given, James, Cephas, and John—those reputed to be pillars—gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
passages.sermon:
James, Cephas, and John were leaders in the church.
People considered them to be pillars.
They saw that God had given grace to me.
They recognized this grace.
They gave the right hand of fellowship to me and Barnabas.
They did this to show agreement and partnership.
They agreed that we should go to the Gentiles.
They themselves would go to the circumcised.
passages.original: καὶ γνόντες τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι Ἰάκωβος καὶ Κηφᾶς καὶ Ἰωάννης οἱ δοκοῦντες στῦλοι εἶναι δεξιὰς ἔδωκαν ἐμοὶ καὶ Βαρνάβα κοινωνίας ἵνα ἡμεῖς εἰς τὰ ἔθνη αὐτοὶ δὲ εἰς τὴν περιτομήν

passages.text: They only asked us to remember the poor, the very thing I was eager to do.
passages.sermon:
James, Cephas, and John asked us to remember the poor.
They wanted us to care for people who had little.
I was eager to do this.
I made every effort to help the poor.
passages.original: μόνον τῶν πτωχῶν ἵνα μνημονεύωμεν ὃ καὶ ἐσπούδασα αὐτὸ τοῦτο ποιῆσαι

passages.text: When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face, because he stood to be condemned.
passages.sermon:
Cephas was a leader among the apostles.
He came to Antioch.
I opposed Cephas directly.
I did this face to face.
Cephas was clearly in the wrong.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν Κηφᾶς εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν κατὰ πρόσωπον αὐτῷ ἀντέστην ὅτι κατεγνωσμένος ἦν

passages.text: For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they arrived, he began to draw back and separate himself, for fear of those in the circumcision group.
passages.sermon:
Cephas was a Jewish Christian leader.
He used to eat with the Gentiles.
This happened before certain men came from James.
When these men arrived, Cephas changed his behavior.
He began to draw back from the Gentiles.
He separated himself from them.
He did this because he was afraid of the circumcision group.
The circumcision group were Jews who insisted on following Jewish customs.
passages.original: πρὸ τοῦ γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τινας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβου μετὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν συνήσθιεν ὅτε δὲ ἦλθον ὑπέστελλεν καὶ ἀφώριζεν ἑαυτόν φοβούμενος τοὺς ἐκ περιτομῆς

passages.text: The other Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray.
passages.sermon: The other Jews saw Cephas separate himself from the Gentiles.\r\nThey also acted hypocritically with him.\r\nEven Barnabas was led astray by their hypocrisy.
passages.original: καὶ συνυπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ Ἰουδαῖοι ὥστε καὶ Βαρνάβας συναπήχθη αὐτῶν τῇ ὑποκρίσει

passages.text: When I saw that they were not walking in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, “If you, who are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul saw a problem.
Some people were not acting according to the truth of the gospel.
Paul spoke to Cephas.
Paul spoke in front of everyone.
Paul said, "You are a Jew."
"You live like a Gentile."
"You do not live like a Jew."
"How can you make Gentiles live like Jews?"
passages.original: Ἀλλ’ ὅτε εἶδον ὅτι οὐκ ὀρθοποδοῦσιν πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου εἶπον τῷ Κηφᾷ ἔμπροσθεν πάντων Εἰ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὑπάρχων ἐθνικῶς καὶ οὐκ Ἰουδαϊκῶς ζῇς πῶς τὰ ἔθνη ἀναγκάζεις ἰουδαΐζειν

passages.text: We who are Jews by birth and not Gentile “sinners” know that a man is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ. So we, too, have believed in Christ Jesus, that we may be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified.
passages.sermon:
We are Jews by birth.
We are not Gentile sinners.
We know something important.
A person is not justified by works of the law.
A person is justified only through faith in Jesus Christ.
We have believed in Christ Jesus.
We did this so that we would be justified by faith in Christ.
We are not justified by works of the law.
No one will be justified by works of the law.
passages.original: Ἡμεῖς φύσει Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἐθνῶν Ἁμαρτωλοί εἰδότες δὲ ὅτι οὐ δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἐὰν μὴ διὰ πίστεως Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπιστεύσαμεν ἵνα δικαιωθῶμεν ἐκ πίστεως Χριστοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σάρξ

passages.text: But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin? Certainly not!
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church about justification in Christ.
Paul and other believers seek to be justified in Christ.
They are found to be sinners while seeking this justification.
Some may ask if this means Christ serves sin.
Paul answers, "Certainly not!"
Christ is not a servant of sin.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ ζητοῦντες δικαιωθῆναι ἐν Χριστῷ εὑρέθημεν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἁμαρτωλοί ἆρα Χριστὸς ἁμαρτίας διάκονος μὴ γένοιτο

passages.text: If I rebuild what I have already torn down, I prove myself to be a lawbreaker.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking about the law and faith in Christ.
Paul says, “If I rebuild what I have already torn down, I show that I am a lawbreaker.”
If I return to the old ways I left behind, I prove I am guilty.
If I try to restore what I destroyed, I show I have broken the law.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ ἃ κατέλυσα ταῦτα πάλιν οἰκοδομῶ παραβάτην ἐμαυτὸν συνιστάνω

passages.text: For through the law I died to the law so that I might live to God.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks here.
\r\nPaul once lived under the law.
\r\nThe law showed Paul his sin.
\r\nBecause of the law, Paul died to the law.
\r\nPaul no longer lives by the law.
\r\nPaul now lives for God.
passages.original: ἐγὼ γὰρ διὰ νόμου νόμῳ ἀπέθανον ἵνα Θεῷ ζήσω

passages.text: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself up for me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul has been crucified with Christ.
\r\nPaul no longer lives for himself.
\r\nChrist lives in Paul.
\r\nPaul now lives his life in his body.
\r\nPaul lives by faith in the Son of God.
\r\nThe Son of God loved Paul.
\r\nThe Son of God gave Himself up for Paul.
passages.original: Χριστῷ συνεσταύρωμαι ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγώ ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ ἐν σαρκί ἐν πίστει ζῶ τῇ τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντός με καὶ παραδόντος ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: I do not set aside the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, Christ died for nothing.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Galatians.
\r\nPaul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul says, "I do not set aside the grace of God."
\r\nGod gives grace.
\r\nIf righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.
\r\nRighteousness does not come through the law.
\r\nChrist died with purpose.
\r\nChrist’s death is not in vain.
passages.original: Οὐκ ἀθετῶ τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰ γὰρ διὰ νόμου δικαιοσύνη ἄρα Χριστὸς δωρεὰν ἀπέθανεν
